section_summary: This section begins with wartime German accounts of patent contracts and technical information supplied to Japan. Postwar correspondence then seeks protection or accounting for American patent rights, licenses, bank deposits, and business interests in Japan and Manchuria. Most of the section is International General Electric material: a statement of its interests in Japan and Korea, followed by two extensive Japanese patent schedules.

subfiles.title: Copies of letters on patent contracts with Japan
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, War Department Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.to: Directors of European and Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards letters concerning German patent contracts with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards attached patent-contract material at the suggestion of the Office of Military Government for Germany.

subfiles.title: Patent Contracts with Japan
subfiles.about: Explains the German Japan Committee’s handling of wartime patent and technical-transfer agreements.
subfiles.summary: Baatz identifies committee members and Japanese negotiators, describes pricing and production disputes, and lists aircraft, weapons, electronics and manufacturing technology sought by Japan. He suggests ways to locate fuller records and offers his assistance.

subfiles.title: Junkers licenses and patents department
subfiles.about: Describes the organization and duties of the Junkers aircraft and engine works’ patent and licensing department.
subfiles.summary: Rosalsky outlines patent examination, protection, administration, licensing and technical reporting across Junkers’ engine, aircraft and special-fields sections. He says a reduced staff continues patent work after plant operations ceased.

subfiles.title: Northern Equipment Company inquiry about Japanese patents and bank deposit
subfiles.about: Requests an accounting of wartime use of its Japanese patents and a Tokyo bank balance.
subfiles.summary: Asks about Japanese manufacturing permits under four patents and funds held at the 100th Bank’s Hibiya branch.

subfiles.title: Instruction to investigate Northern Equipment Company patent permits
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests investigation and protection of Northern Equipment Company’s Japanese patent interests.
subfiles.summary: Directs the Political Adviser to investigate alleged wartime permits and report findings for the company.

subfiles.title: Reply to Northern Equipment Company
subfiles.from: Benedict N. English, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: E. W. Scarlett, Northern Equipment Company
subfiles.about: Seeks sworn company and bank-deposit information while arranging an investigation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests sworn statements on the company’s ownership, patent claim and Tokyo bank deposit. Reports that the Political Adviser has been asked to investigate.

subfiles.title: La Mont Corporation request to protect Japanese patent and license rights
subfiles.from: Warren I. Lee, La Mont Corporation
subfiles.to: Department of State, Japanese and Korean Economic Division
subfiles.about: Asks how to send an agent to investigate suspected boiler-patent infringement in Japan and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Seeks licensing guidance to investigate infringement, protect patents and agreements, and restore markets.

subfiles.title: Reply to La Mont Corporation on business licenses and patent protection
subfiles.from: Roswell U. Whitman, Department of State
subfiles.to: Warren I. Lee, La Mont Corporation
subfiles.about: Explains current restrictions on business activity in occupied Japan and the status of Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Says Treasury licenses are unavailable for Japan; SCAP is protecting Allied interests. Manchuria requires no special license.

subfiles.title: International General Electric interests in Japan and Korea
subfiles.about: Asserts patent, trademark, shareholding and property interests affected by wartime Japanese measures.
subfiles.summary: International General Electric claims assignment or licensing rights in patents registered through Japanese partners and an interest in Osram patents and trademarks. It details its Tokyo-Shibaura shares, their wartime sale, and related company interests. It asks the Department to safeguard those interests and alert American representatives before property is disposed of.

subfiles.title: Interest in Companies in which Enemy Interests were known to exist: Japan and Korea
subfiles.about: Details patent rights, Tokyo-Shibaura holdings, subsidiaries and principal works in Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: The statement explains claimed rights to General Electric and Osram patents, applications and trademarks, plus International General Electric’s former Tokyo-Shibaura voting and financial interests. It lists Japanese and Korean companies linked to Tokyo-Shibaura and schedules its principal works, locations and products.

subfiles.title: Japan: Patents on G.E. Inventions Assigned to Shibaura Co.
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese patents on General Electric inventions assigned to Shibaura.
subfiles.summary: Forty-one pages tabulate patent numbers, publication and grant dates, invention titles, and General Electric docket numbers. The inventions span electrical power and control, machinery, refrigeration, materials, communications and other technologies.

subfiles.title: Japan: Patents on G.E. Inventions Assigned to Tokyo Co.
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese patents on General Electric inventions assigned to Tokyo Electric Company.
subfiles.summary: The schedule tabulates patent numbers, dates, titles and docket numbers, chiefly for lamps, electric discharge devices, radio, signaling, optics and related equipment. It continues beyond page 79.
